transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I’m having trouble following through on things. I’ll start follow-up items after audits or mentorship events, and I really do mean to finish them, but then a few days later I realize the final email, review note, or form never actually got done. It’s been happening enough that I felt like I needed to talk to someone about it.
Have you had this kind of trouble finishing tasks since you were a child?

Yes, it goes back pretty far. Even in elementary school, my report cards would say things like I was bright, but I lost assignments or rushed through and missed little details. I also remember getting reminders to finish my work and getting in trouble for talking out of turn. My mom still jokes that I could do well on a test but forget the project that was sitting right in my backpack.
Do these same kinds of problems happen outside of work too, like at home or in your personal life?

Yes, it does. At home it’s been a problem too. My husband has had to take over things like bills or commitments I said I would handle, because I just don’t finish them reliably.

And at work, it’s gotten more serious than just being annoying. My mistakes and unfinished follow-up affected a client review, and now I’m worried people are wondering if I can really handle the promotion.
Have you been feeling depressed most days?
I don’t think so, no. I get frustrated and worried about the mistakes, but I wouldn’t say I feel depressed most days.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on a task, even when you want to get it done?

Yes. I can start out really focused, like in a long client meeting or a training on one of the AI tools, and I’m paying attention at first. But after a while my mind just kind of drifts, and then I realize I’ve missed the last few minutes, even though I’m still sitting there looking at the screen.
Do you often feel restless, like it’s hard to sit still?

Yes. Sitting through a long review can feel almost physically uncomfortable, like this pressure building up inside. I’ll start needing to stand up or move around, even if there’s no real reason—like walking to the printer or finding some excuse to get out of my chair for a minute.
Have these attention and follow-through problems caused serious problems in your life, like at work or in your relationships?

Yes, it has. At work it’s gotten more serious than just little annoyances. I’ve made mistakes and left follow-up unfinished, and it actually affected a client review. Since I got promoted, I worry people are starting to wonder if I can really handle it.

And at home, my husband has had to step in with bills and things I agreed to do, because he can’t really count on me to finish them reliably. That’s been hard to admit.
Were these attention and follow-through problems already causing noticeable trouble before your recent promotion?

Yes, looking back, it was there long before the promotion. Even in elementary school my report cards would say I was bright, but I lost assignments, rushed through small details, talked out of turn, and needed reminders to finish my work. My mom still jokes that I could ace a test but forget the project sitting in my backpack.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different things?
I’m not sure I’d say I worry about lots of different things all the time. I do get concerned when something is hanging over me, but I haven’t really noticed constant worrying across everything.
Do these attention and follow-through problems happen in more than one part of your life, not just at work?

Yes, definitely. It’s not just at work. Work is where it’s become more obvious, like with the client review and worrying people think I can’t handle the promotion. But at home it shows up too—my husband has had to take over bills and other things I said I’d do because he can’t really rely on me to finish them.
